chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated to us from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i al-Qadi. He said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) say:

Iblis came to Musa ibn 'Imran (peace be upon him) while he was communing with his Lord. An angel from the angels said to him: What do you hope to gain from him while he is in this state, communing with his Lord? He said: I hope to gain from him what I hoped to gain from his father Adam when he was in Paradise.

Among what Allah the Exalted communicated to him was that He said to him: O Musa! I do not accept prayer except from one who humbles himself before My greatness, attaches his heart to the fear of Me, spends his day in My remembrance, does not sleep while persisting in sin, and recognizes the right of My friends and My beloved ones.

Musa said: O Lord! By Your beloved ones and Your friends, do You mean Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Ya'qub? He (Mighty and Majestic) said: They are that, O Musa, but I was referring to the one for whose sake I created Adam and Hawwa', and for whose sake I created Paradise and the Fire. Musa said: And who is he, O Lord? He said: Muhammad, Ahmad — I derived his name from My name, for I am the Praised (al-Mahmud). Musa said: O Lord! Make me of his nation. He said: You, O Musa, are of his nation if you recognize him and recognize his station and the station of his Ahl al-Bayt. Verily, his likeness and the likeness of his Ahl al-Bayt...

Verily, his likeness and the likeness of his Ahl al-Bayt among those I have created is like the likeness of al-Firdaws in the gardens — its leaves do not dry up and its taste does not change. Whoever recognizes them and recognizes their right, I shall grant him forbearance in moments of ignorance and a light in moments of darkness. I will answer him before he calls out to Me, and I will give to him before he asks Me.

O Musa, when you see poverty approaching, say: Welcome, O emblem of the righteous! And when you see wealth approaching, say: This is a sin whose punishment has been hastened. Indeed, this world is the abode of punishment — in it I punished Adam for his sin. I have made it cursed, and cursed is whatever is in it, except what is devoted to Me. O Musa, My righteous servants have renounced it in proportion to their knowledge of Me, while the rest of My creation have coveted it in proportion to their ignorance of Me. There is no one among My creation who has glorified it but that his eye was gladdened [with grief], and none has held it in contempt but that he benefited from it.

Then al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: If you are able not to be recognized [by people], then do so. What harm is it to you if the people do not praise you? And what harm is it to you if you are condemned in the eyes of people, so long as you are praised in the sight of Allah? Indeed, 'Ali, peace be upon him, used to say: There is no good in this world except for one of two men — a man who increases in goodness every day, and a man who makes up for his sin through repentance. But how is repentance [available] to him? By Allah, even if he prostrates until his neck breaks, Allah will not accept from him unless it is through our walaya, O People of the Household.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: Ahl al-Bayt: the Prophet's household, the Imams
key_terms.الْفِرْدَوْسُ: Al-Firdaws: the highest garden in Paradise
key_terms.شِعَارُ الصَّالِحِينَ: The emblem/motto of the righteous — poverty as a spiritual mark
key_terms.وَلَايَة: Walaya: devotion, guardianship and spiritual allegiance to the Imams
key_terms.يُنَاجِي: Communing privately with God; intimate divine dialogue

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the status of Prophet Muhammad and the Ahl al-Bayt in the sight of Allah?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and Hafs ibn Ghiyath, relates a divine dialogue between Allah and Prophet Musa (AS) in which Satan's ambitions are exposed and the supreme station of the Prophet Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt is proclaimed. God declares that He created the universe for the sake of the Prophet, whose name derives from the Divine Name al-Mahmud, and conditions acceptance of prayer upon humility, godconsciousness, and recognition of the Ahl al-Bayt's rights. The hadith concludes with Imam al-Sadiq's exhortations on obscurity, renunciation of the world, and the indispensability of walaya (guardianship/allegiance) of the Ahl al-Bayt for the acceptance of deeds.
